# Auto-generated software tools tables

`docs/intro.mdx` has four "Software tools" tables, one per category —
**Libraries**, **ROS**, **Simulation**, **Other** — each listing every
product that has a tool in that category, with each cell showing that
tool's support badge linked to its page. Every category is built the
same way: one column per distinct tool `title` found under that
category's leaf pages. `ROS` columns happen to always collapse to a
single one, `ROS`, because a product gets at most one `Category-ROS`
page — there's no `ROS1`/`ROS2` split any more, and no per-distro split
either (which specific ROS distros a driver supports is that driver's
own repo README's job, not this site's) — but the mechanism itself is
the same generic one every other category uses, no special-casing in the
script.

**Libraries / ROS / Simulation / Other** all get the same table again,
single-row versions scoped to just that product, on that product's own
`software-tools/<Product>/index.mdx`. **Libraries / Simulation / Other**
additionally get it a third time, once the product actually has a tool
there, on that category's own dedicated `<Category>/index.mdx` landing
page. **`ROS` is the one exception**: it never gets a dedicated landing
page, because a product's `ROS/index.mdx` is already the real content
page (synced from a driver's README, or hand-authored for a third-party
integration) — not a container with multiple possible tools to summarize.
You never edit any of these tables by hand — all of them are regenerated
by
[`scripts/generate-tools-table.js`](https://github.com/robotiq/robotiq.github.io/blob/main/scripts/generate-tools-table.js),
which runs automatically on `npm start` / `npm run build` (same as
`sync-external-docs.js`).

The script walks each `software-tools/<Product>/` folder tree looking for
tool leaf pages — an `index.mdx` carrying a `Category` badge — regardless
of how deeply it's nested (`Libraries/`, `ROS/`, `Simulation/`, `Other/`, or
no container folder at all). Every product lives there, versioned or not
— see [Documentation versioning](./versioning) for why. For each leaf
page found:

- **Row** — the product's own `title` frontmatter (from
  `software-tools/<Product>/index.mdx`).
- **Column** — the tool's own `title` frontmatter (e.g. `Python`, or
  `ROS` for the one `ROS` leaf a product can have).
- **Cell** — the tool's `Supported_by-<Label>-<color>` badge, shown
  compactly (no "Supported by" prefix — only the source page keeps the
  full badge), linking to that tool's own page.

A page can carry extra badges beyond `Category`/`Supported_by` — e.g. a
page documenting an archived, no-longer-maintained driver could add
`![Legacy](.../badge/Status-Legacy-000000)` next to its (accurate)
`Supported_by-Third_party` badge. Only `Supported_by-` feeds the tables, so
any other `badge/<Key>-<Value>-<color>` (a different key, not `Supported_by`)
shows on that tool's own page without ever leaking into the summary tables —
useful for a status that's real but not "who maintains it," which is all
the tables are meant to answer.

This means adding a new product or tool page, with a title and the right
badges, is enough to make it appear in the matching tables on the next
build — no manual edit needed. A category with no products yet writes
nothing between its markers at all — heading included — so the whole
section disappears from the page rather than sitting there empty under a
heading with no content.

A few things are still hand-maintained in the script itself, by design —
they're presentation choices, not derivable from the file tree:

- `COLUMN_ORDER` — preferred left-to-right order for each category's
  columns. Anything not listed still gets its own column, just sorted
  alphabetically after the known ones.
- `COLUMN_DESCRIPTIONS` — the one-line legend shown under each table. A
  column missing here still appears, just with no legend line, until one
  is added.

To test a change locally:

```bash
node scripts/generate-tools-table.js
```

It rewrites the content between each `AUTO-GENERATED-<CATEGORY>-TABLE`
marker pair (`AUTO-GENERATED-LIBRARIES-TABLE`, `AUTO-GENERATED-ROS-TABLE`,
`AUTO-GENERATED-SIMULATION-TABLE`, `AUTO-GENERATED-OTHER-TABLE`) in
`docs/intro.mdx`, the *same* marker pair again on each product's own
`index.mdx` (every category gets the same inline single-row summary
there), and — for `Libraries`/`Simulation`/`Other`, once a product
actually has any tool pages in that category — the same marker pair a
third time on that category's own dedicated `<Category>/index.mdx`
sub-page. `ROS` is excluded from that third step (see above): its
`ROS/index.mdx` already exists as the real content page, with no
auto-generated table of its own to fill in.

The category's own heading (e.g. `### Libraries`, `### ROS`) is written
*inside* the marker pair, not hand-authored above it, specifically so a
category with zero tool pages for a given product can disappear
entirely — heading and all — rather than leaving a heading that titles an
empty section. That product never gets a sub-page at all either (see
[Adding a new software tool](./adding-a-tool#4-create-the-product-landing-page)).
If a product has tool pages in `Libraries`/`Simulation`/`Other` but no
matching `<Category>/index.mdx` with those markers, the script throws a
build error naming the missing file rather than silently skipping it.

The (up to three) destinations use different link styles on purpose:
`docs/intro.mdx` needs root-relative links (`drivers/<Product>/<Tool>`); a
product's own `index.mdx` needs page-relative links (`<Tool>`); a
category's own dedicated sub-page needs links relative to *that* page
(`<Tool>`, one level deeper than the product root, since every one of
these sub-pages lives one level below the product's own `index.mdx`).
Reusing the wrong style would silently double or misalign the path — the
script keeps these as separate href fields (`href`, `localHref`,
`categoryLocalHref`) to avoid that. `ROS` only ever uses the first two —
`categoryLocalHref` is computed for it like any other tool but never
read, since it has no dedicated sub-page to link from.

## A tool page's own sub-section list

A tool page that's been [split into overview, API reference, and
guides](./how-it-works#splitting-a-tool-page-into-overview-api-reference-and-guides)
also gets its own auto-generated list, right on `<Tool>/index.mdx`, linking
to whichever of those sub-sections actually exist — rendered as boxes
(`.subpage-link` in `src/css/custom.css`, the graphic chart's own
documented "text in blue box" emphasis style) rather than a plain bullet
list. Two independent things use the same mechanism:

- **A tool's own sub-sections** — `collectSubpages` looks at a tool's
  immediate subdirectories for one that has its own index page (`.mdx`, or
  `.md` for doxygen2docusaurus's generated `API/index.md`) but carries no
  `Category` badge of its own — i.e. it's a sub-section of this tool, not a
  different tool. Generic, not hardcoded to `API`/`docs`: any folder
  matching that shape becomes an entry, labeled from its own `title`
  frontmatter (except `API/`, which always shows "API Reference" — that
  generated page's own title is long and product-specific, so this matches
  the fixed label `sidebars.software-tools.js` already uses for it via
  `doxygenApiCategory`). Order follows `SUBPAGE_ORDER` in the script
  (guides before the generated API reference, matching
  `sidebars.software-tools.js`'s own convention) — a folder not listed
  there still appears, just sorted alphabetically after the known ones.
  **Its `href` always ends with a trailing slash** (`docs/`, not `docs`) —
  load-bearing, not cosmetic: this renders as a raw `<a href>`, not a
  Docusaurus `<Link>`, so a click resolves it with plain browser
  relative-URL rules, not anything Docusaurus-aware. Every one of these
  entries points at a folder's own index page; without the trailing slash,
  landing there leaves the browser one segment short of that page's real
  URL, and any *further* relative link clicked from it (e.g. one of that
  folder's own guide tiles, below) resolves against the wrong base and
  silently 404s — confirmed the hard way, via exactly that chain. See
  `test/subpage-links.test.js` for the regression test.
- **A guide folder's own contents** — the same mechanism runs again, one
  level deeper, on a guide folder's *own* `docs/index.mdx` (or equivalent),
  this time via `collectFolderGuides`: the guide files themselves (e.g.
  `01-environment-setup.md`), ordered the same way
  [`folder-sidebar.mjs`](./how-it-works#splitting-a-tool-page-into-overview-api-reference-and-guides)
  orders them in the sidebar (`sidebar_position` frontmatter, else
  filename), labeled from `sidebar_label`/`title` frontmatter or — since a
  synced guide usually has neither — its own first `# Heading`, matching
  Docusaurus's own fallback for a page with no frontmatter title. A folder
  with no sibling guide files (e.g. the generated `API/` folder, whose only
  children are subfolders like `classes/`/`groups/`) yields an empty list,
  same as a tool with no sub-sections.

Both are self-installing: unlike the category tables above, the
`AUTO-GENERATED-SUBPAGES-TABLE`/`AUTO-GENERATED-GUIDES-TABLE` marker pair
isn't expected to pre-exist on every page — most pages will never have
anything to list, and an always-empty marker block on each of them would
be pure clutter. The first time a page actually has something to list, the
script inserts the marker itself — right after a `## Contents` heading if
the page already has one (prepare this heading wherever you want the list
to land), else right after the page's badges, else right after its
frontmatter — and keeps the block up to date after that (never deleting the
marker itself). Once the marker exists, you're free to move it (and its
surrounding heading) anywhere else on the page — the script only ever
rewrites what's *between* the markers, never their position.

Both lists are derived from gitignored, sync-generated folders (a tool's
`API/index.md`, a guide folder's own `.md` files) — genuinely absent on a
fresh clone before the first full build, or after a Doxygen failure
`sync-external-docs.js` warned-and-continued through. To avoid wiping real,
committed content over a transient local gap like that, an empty result
here only ever *fills* a previously-empty block, never empties an
already non-empty one — a page that finds nothing to list this run, but
whose tracked block isn't already empty, is left untouched (with a console
warning) instead. A guide or API reference genuinely, permanently removed
upstream still needs a one-time manual edit to clear the stale list here —
the same way a reviewer would catch any other stale content in the diff.
